name: AgentOS
tag: Coordinates many engineering agents on one visual board so work moves without collisions.

scenarios.title: Ship a feature with an agent team
scenarios.ask: Build the saved-search feature with {agents} coding agents across {repos} repos, with {gate} review.
steps: Planner
Broke the feature into {=6 + repos * 3} tasks and drew them as a workflow graph.
Dispatcher
Gave each of the {agents} agents its own branch and file lock so no two edit the same file.
Test agent
Ran tests after every task. {=max(1, round((6 + repos * 3) * 0.15))} tasks failed once and were retried.
Integrator
Merged branches in dependency order. Review gate: {gate}.
Board
Updated the visual board live so the lead sees what is blocked.

result.title: Feature status
rows: about {=round((6 + repos * 3) / min(agents, 6 + repos * 3) * 25 + gate * 30)} minutes

followups: What stops agents from overwriting each other?
File locks and separate branches. If two tasks need the same file, the Dispatcher runs them one after the other.
Can a person take over a task?
Yes. Drag the task to your name on the board and the agent stops and hands over its notes.

scenarios.title: Clear a bug backlog
scenarios.ask: We have {bugs} open bugs. Let agents fix the easy ones and leave the rest triaged.
steps: Triage agent
Sorted {bugs} bugs: {=round(bugs * 0.35)} small, {=round(bugs * 0.4)} medium, {=bugs - round(bugs * 0.35) - round(bugs * 0.4)} need a person.
Dispatcher
Queued small bugs to {agents} agents, one bug per branch.
Fixer agents
Wrote a fix and a failing-then-passing test for each.
Reviewer
Opened {=round(bugs * 0.3)} pull requests. {=round(bugs * 0.05)} small bugs were not reproducible and went back to triage.
followups: Small bugs have clear repro steps and limited scope, so an agent's fix is easy to check. Bigger ones get a triage note to speed up the person who takes them.
Does every fix come with a test?
Yes. A fix without a test that fails before and passes after is not submitted.

scenarios.title: Upgrade a framework
scenarios.ask: Upgrade our framework one major version across {services} services.
steps: Planner
Ordered {services} services by dependency so shared libraries go first.
Workflow
Built a reusable upgrade workflow: bump, fix breaking calls, run tests, open a pull request.
Agents
Ran the workflow on {agents} services at a time.
Watcher
Paused {=max(1, round(services * 0.1))} services that failed integration tests and attached the error summary.
followups: Can we run it on a schedule?
Yes. The upgrade workflow is saved, so it can run each time a new minor version ships.
What if a service has no tests?
The workflow marks it high risk and asks a person to approve before merging.
